t: You're looking at the Gielgud Theatre, a West End house on Shaftesbury Avenue at the corner of Rupert Street. It has nine hundred and ninety-four seats on three levels. It was designed by W. G. R. Sprague, who designed at least thirty-five theatres between 1890 and 1929. The theatre is named for Sir John Gielgud, whose career spanned eight decades and who, with Olivier, Redgrave and Richardson, dominated the British stage of the mid-twentieth century.
